name: resnet
description: Generation evaluation on a real paper: He et al., Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (CVPR 2016). The PDF is not versioned; pass its folder with --papers-dir. Pages are 1-based PDF pages. Evidence quotes are matched ignoring whitespace and case; facts list accepted alternatives and every group must appear for a correct answer.

documents.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

cases.question: Which problem do the authors address by introducing the deep residual learning framework?
cases.reference_answer: The degradation problem: as plain networks get deeper, accuracy saturates and then degrades and the training error grows; it is not caused by overfitting.

evidence.text: we address the degradation problem by introducing a deep residual learning framework
a degradation problem has been exposed

cases.question: What mini-batch size was used to train the ImageNet models?
cases.reference_answer: 256 (SGD with a mini-batch size of 256); the CIFAR-10 models used 128.

evidence.text: use SGD with a mini-batch size of 256

cases.question: Which weight decay and momentum were used to train on ImageNet?
cases.reference_answer: Weight decay of 0.0001 and momentum of 0.9.

evidence.text: use a weight decay of 0.0001 and a momentum of 0.9

cases.question: What top-5 error did the ResNet ensemble obtain on the ImageNet test set?
cases.reference_answer: 3.57% top-5 error, which won the 1st place in the ILSVRC 2015 classification task.

evidence.text: An ensemble of these residual nets achieves 3.57% error on the ImageNet test set
Our ensemble has 3.57% top-5 error
This leads to 3.57% top-5 error on the test set

cases.question: Which layers make up the bottleneck building block used in ResNet-50/101/152?
cases.reference_answer: A stack of three convolutions, 1×1, 3×3 and 1×1; the 1×1 layers reduce and then restore the dimensions.

evidence.text: The three layers are 1×1, 3×3, and 1×1 convolutions

cases.question: What relative improvement on the COCO object detection dataset do the deep residual representations bring?
cases.reference_answer: A 28% relative improvement (+6.0 points in COCO's mAP@[.5, .95]).

evidence.text: we obtain a 28% relative improvement on the COCO object detection dataset
which is a 28% relative improvement

cases.question: What is the main idea of this paper?
cases.reference_answer: Let stacked layers learn a residual function F(x) = H(x) - x through identity shortcut connections, which makes much deeper networks easier to optimize.

evidence.text: reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs
we explicitly let these layers fit a residual mapping

cases.question: Why do deeper networks sometimes perform worse?
cases.reference_answer: Degradation: with more depth, accuracy saturates and then degrades and the training error increases; it is an optimization difficulty, not overfitting.

evidence.text: such degradation is not caused by overfitting
accuracy gets saturated (which might be unsurprising) and then degrades rapidly

cases.question: Did the method win any competition?
cases.reference_answer: Yes: 1st place in the ILSVRC 2015 classification task, and also ImageNet detection, ImageNet localization, COCO detection and COCO segmentation.

evidence.text: This result won the 1st place on the ILSVRC 2015 classification task
won the 1st place in the ILSVRC 2015 classification competition
This entry won the 1st place in ILSVRC 2015
we won the 1st places in several tracks in ILSVRC & COCO 2015 competitions

cases.question: How do the shortcut connections work?
cases.reference_answer: They skip one or more layers and perform identity mapping; their outputs are added to the outputs of the stacked layers, with no extra parameters or computation.

evidence.text: the shortcut connections simply perform identity mapping, and their outputs are added to the outputs of the stacked layers

cases.question: According to Table 2, what is the top-1 error of the 34-layer plain network?
cases.reference_answer: 28.54% (top-1, 10-crop testing, ImageNet validation).

cases.question: What top-5 error does ResNet-50 reach in Table 3 (10-crop testing)?
On CIFAR-10 (Table 6), what error does the 110-layer ResNet reach and how many parameters does it have?
cases.reference_answer: 6.43% error (best of 5 runs; mean 6.61±0.16) with 1.7M parameters.

evidence.text: ResNet 110 1.7M 6.43

cases.question: In Table 8, what mAP@[.5, .95] does ResNet-101 achieve on the COCO validation set?
How many FLOPs does the 152-layer ResNet have?
cases.reference_answer: 11.3 billion FLOPs, still fewer than VGG-16/19 (15.3/19.6 billion).

evidence.text: the 152-layer ResNet (11.3 billion FLOPs)

cases.question: Qual é o erro top-5 do ResNet-152 como modelo único na validação do ImageNet?
cases.reference_answer: 4,49% (Tabela 4); esse modelo único supera todos os ensembles anteriores.

evidence.text: single-model top-5 validation error of 4.49%

cases.question: Que problema aparece quando se aumenta a profundidade de redes planas, sem atalhos?
cases.reference_answer: O problema de degradação: a acurácia satura e depois cai, e o erro de treino aumenta; não é causado por overfitting.

evidence.text: such degradation is not caused by overfitting
34-layer plain net has higher training error throughout the whole training procedure

cases.question: Qual é a taxa de aprendizado inicial no treino do ImageNet e como ela muda?
cases.reference_answer: Começa em 0,1 e é dividida por 10 quando o erro estabiliza.

evidence.text: The learning rate starts from 0.1 and is divided by 10 when the error plateaus

cases.question: Quantas imagens de treino e de teste tem o CIFAR-10 usado no artigo?
cases.reference_answer: 50 mil imagens de treino e 10 mil de teste, em 10 classes.

evidence.text: which consists of 50k training images and 10k testing images in 10 classes

cases.question: Qual é a diferença entre os atalhos do ResNet e os das highway networks?
cases.reference_answer: As highway networks usam portas (gating) que dependem dos dados e têm parâmetros, e podem se fechar; os atalhos identidade do ResNet não têm parâmetros e nunca se fecham.

evidence.text: present shortcut connections with gating functions
in contrast to our identity shortcuts that are parameter-free

cases.question: O que é a opção B de atalhos no artigo?
cases.reference_answer: Atalhos de projeção (convoluções 1×1) apenas quando as dimensões aumentam; os demais atalhos são identidade.

evidence.text: (B) projection shortcuts are used for increasing dimensions, and other shortcuts are identity
(B) The projection shortcut in Eqn.(2) is used to match dimensions

cases.question: What BLEU score does the model achieve on WMT14 English-German translation?
cases.reference_answer: Not in the paper: it has no machine translation experiments.

cases.question: How many parameters does the 152-layer ResNet have?
cases.reference_answer: Not in the paper: it reports only FLOPs for ResNet-152 (11.3 billion); parameter counts are given only for the CIFAR-10 models.

cases.question: Quantas horas levou o treinamento do ResNet-152 no ImageNet?
cases.reference_answer: O artigo não informa o tempo de treinamento.

cases.question: Qual foi a acurácia do ResNet no conjunto de teste do MNIST?
cases.reference_answer: O artigo não informa; o MNIST só aparece ao citar o trabalho [41].

cases.question: Como o artigo compara as ResNets com os Vision Transformers?
cases.reference_answer: Não compara; os Vision Transformers são posteriores ao artigo (2016).
